title: Installing a Woodworking Vice on a Workbench
excerpt: A practical upgrade to any workbench: installing a 7" woodworking vice for improved clamping and precision work.
body:
## Overview One of the upgrades I wanted to make to my workbench was installing a woodworking vice. This type of vice is a practical and essential addition for any workshop, making clamping, holding, and precision work much easier. ## Why Install a Vice A good woodworking vice significantly improves accuracy and control when cutting, sanding, or assembling parts. The model used in this build is a classic 7" (175 mm) woodworking vice, known for its durability, ease of installation, and solid clamping force. ## Installation The installation process is simple and can be done with basic tools: - Position the vice under the workbench top - Mark and drill the mounting holes - Secure it using bolts or heavy-duty screws Most workbenches can accommodate this type of vice with minimal adjustment. ## Custom Jaws To improve performance, wooden jaws can be added. These help: - Protect delicate workpieces - Increase clamping surface - Improve grip on irregular shapes ## Final Result After installation, the workbench becomes much more functional and efficient for everyday tasks. This upgrade is simple, affordable and has a significant impact on workflow. ## Image Gallery
